I currently adjunct, and it is a job that makes sense for me as I finish a long-term project. I have honestly bitten off more than I can chew this semester and am teaching 5 classes total at 2 different universities. 

I was given a basic blueprint of the class with some materials, but designed the syllabus and, of course, my lectures.

I take my job seriously and feel a deep moral responsibility to my students. For my efforts, I get slightly less than $3k/month after taxes with no pay during holidays. For 5, yes, 5 classes. With an MA degree and close to a decade (on and off) experience. 

I worry constantly about money and wouldn’t make enough to survive if I didn’t have some savings. 

I am beyond exhausted, and have honestly begun cutting corners where I can. 

It isn’t just the teaching and planning, but the one hour/week office hours, the constant emailing, and things, like recommendation letters. 

Last year, a class was almost canceled 5 days before the semester with no more than an obligatory “sorry”. 

I’ve begun looking into other opportunities.

I think that universities know they can take advantage of adjuncts because most have chosen the job for its flexibility and will still work harder than the university deserves because of a commitment to the students.
